verdict:
# K.16980 and Gilgameš Tablet I

**Verdict:** Yes. K.16980 fits Tablet I at **lines 220–221**, in Enkidu's boastful speech to Šamḫat just before he sets out for Uruk. This is the placement the scholar's note ("cf. Gilg I 222–223") points to; the line numbers are offset by two, probably from an older edition. The fit is strong for fragment line 2 and for the key word in fragment line 1. The sign just before that word is a problem, discussed below.

## 1. What the fragment preserves

| Fragment | Signs | Likely normalisation |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | [... i?-s]in-nu ši-ma-t[u₂? ...] | ... *šīmātu* ... |
| 2 | [...] x EDIN al-du [...] | ... *ṣēri aldu* ... "(who was) born in the wild" |

Line 2 is the more diagnostic of the two. Birth "in the wild" (*ina ṣēri*) is Enkidu's defining epithet in Tablet I.

## 2. Matching passage in the canonical text

- **Line 220:** *[ ... ] ... šīmata? unakkar*
  - NinNA1a v 22: [x x]-um-ma **ši-ma!?-tu₂** [x x x]
  - NinNA3 v 2: [x x x x **ši-ma!?]-tu₂** u₂-nak-kar
- **Line 221:** *[ša in]a ṣēri iʾʾaldu dān emūqī īšu*
  - NinNA1a v 23: [ša₂ i-n]a **EDIN# iʾ-al-du** [x x x x x x x]
  - NinNA3 v 3: [x x x x x x da-a]n i-mu-qi₂ i-šu

These are the only two adjacent lines in Tablet I with *šīmātu* followed by *ina ṣēri (i)aldu*. The closest competitor is line 226 (*šakin isinnu*), but line 227 (*ašar urtaṣṣanū alû*) has no *ṣēru* or *aldu*, so it fails.

## 3. Sign-by-sign alignment

**Fragment line 1 = line 220**
- ši-ma-t[u₂] corresponds directly to NinNA1a's ši-ma!?-tu₂.
- The following [...] would contain u₂-nak-kar.
- This matters for the text itself. Both Nineveh copies mark the MA as doubtful (!?), and Nurullin proposes reading *ši-giš-tu₂* instead. A third Kuyunjik witness with a clean ši-ma-t[u₂] would support the reading *šīmātu*.

**Fragment line 2 = line 221**
- The damaged "x" before EDIN fits the end of **i-n]a**. Its traces should be checked against NA.
- **al-du** is simply a variant spelling of iʾ-al-du. The same alternation appears within Tablet I itself at line 47 (KalNA1 iʾ-al-du, BabNB2 al-du).
- The break at the right would have held *dān emūqī īšu*.
- The break at the left would have held *ša*.

## 4. The problem in fragment line 1

Before ši-ma-t[u₂], the fragment has ...-in-nu, which the editor restores tentatively as [i?-s]in-nu. NinNA1a instead shows [x x]-**um-ma** there. Three explanations are possible:
- **A genuine variant.** K.16980 would then be a different manuscript with a different word before *šīmātu*. The opening of line 220 is broken in every witness, so this cannot be excluded.
- **A misreading.** The signs before ši-ma-t[u₂] may need collation. The restoration "isinnu" is marked uncertain and may be influenced by *isinnu* in line 226.
- **A different line layout.** Reading [da]n-nu would give the end of line 219 (*anākū-mi dannu*) on the same line as line 220. That would require the fragment to skip the opening [x x]-um-ma of line 220. This is unlikely.

This discrepancy lowers confidence slightly. It does not overturn the identification, because *šīmātu* followed by *ina ṣēri aldu* is too distinctive to be a coincidence.

## 5. Which manuscript it could belong to

NinNA1a and NinNA3 already preserve these lines, so K.16980 must come from another Nineveh copy. Two known manuscripts are broken at about this point and are candidates for testing, though neither can be confirmed without physical collation:
- **NinNA2a:** column iv breaks after line 203, and column v resumes around line 240, so lines 220–221 would fall at the end of col. iv or the top of col. v.
- **NinNA1b:** column v is preserved only to line 212 (v 14), so lines 220–221 would fall around v 22–23.

## Conclusion

K.16980 is a duplicate of SB Gilgameš I 220–221:
- line 1′: [... ] ši-ma-t[u₂ u₂-nak-kar]
- line 2′: [ša i-n]a EDIN al-du [dan e-mu-qi₂ i-šu]

It supports the reading *šīmātu* in line 220 and gives a spelling variant *aldu* for *iʾʾaldu* in line 221. The sign sequence before *šīmātu* ([i?-s]in-nu versus NinNA1a's -um-ma) should be collated.

# K.16980 and Tablet VII: no convincing placement

**Conclusion:** K.16980 does not plausibly belong to any preserved or partly preserved passage of Tablet VII. Its two lines most likely duplicate Tablet I, around lines 221–223, as the file note "cf. Gilg I 222–223" suggests. I have not checked the Tablet I wording against a published edition, so treat that identification as probable, not verified.

## 1. What the fragment preserves

| Line | Signs | Likely reading |
|---|---|---|
| 1′ | [... i?-s]in-nu ši-ma-t[u₂? ...] | …-*nu* followed by *šīmātu* ("destinies"). The restoration *isinnu* ("festival") is marked as doubtful. |
| 2′ | [...] x EDIN al-du [...] | *ša ina* **ṣēri aldu**, "(he) who was born in the steppe", an epithet of Enkidu |

The key diagnostic is **EDIN al-du**. The phrase belongs to Enkidu's self-description as the creature born in the wild.

## 2. Scanning Tablet VII for candidate gaps

**Passages with *šīmtu* or *isinnu* vocabulary**

- **Ll. 102–103** (*šīmata lušīmki / šīmat lā iqattû*) and **l. 151** (*šīmata lušīmki*). These use the singular *šīmata/šīmat* in the formula "I will fix a destiny for you". Neither is followed by anything like *ina ṣēri aldu*. Line 103 is continued by *luzzurki izra rabâ*, which is well preserved in five manuscripts.
- **L. 110** (*lubār isinnātīki*). This is spelled *i-sin-na-ti-ki*, which is incompatible with …*-nu ši-ma-tu*. The next line (111, *u banâti*) also cannot accommodate EDIN al-du.

**Passages with *ṣēru* (EDIN)**

- **L. 131** (*ina ṣērīya*, EDIN-ia): the possessive form, with no *aldu*.
- **L. 147** (*irappud ṣ[ēra]*, E[DIN]): the line ends there, so there is no room for *aldu*.
- None of the preserved Šamaš speech (ll. 134–147) refers to Enkidu as "born in the steppe".

**Wholly lost stretches**

These are ll. 2–26, 179–181, 209–219, 227–248 and 268–297. A two-line scrap with no overlap could in theory sit in any of them. However:
- nothing in those contexts (the gods' council, the dream of the Netherworld, the deathbed) positively predicts the sequence "…destinies / born in the steppe";
- a placement there would be unfalsifiable guesswork, not a join.

## 3. Why Tablet I is the better home

In SB Tablet I, Enkidu announces that he will go to Uruk and challenge Gilgameš. From memory, the relevant lines run approximately:

- **I 221:** "[I will enter and] change the destinies" (*šīmātu … lušanni*).
- **I 222–223:** "[He who] was born in the wild (*ina ṣēri aldu*) [is mighty], he has strength."

Against the fragment:
- **Line 1′** …*-nu ši-ma-t[u₂]* would match the *šīmātu* clause. The doubtful "[i?-s]in-nu" would then be a trace of the verb, or possibly of the adjacent festival (*isinnu*) lines in Šamḫat's description of Uruk. The exact word order in I 221 should be checked against George's edition.
- **Line 2′** …EDIN al-du matches *[ša ina] ṣēri aldu* directly.

The two words keep the same order as the fragment, on consecutive lines. That is exactly what one expects from a Kuyunjik duplicate of Tablet I.

## 4. Verdict

- **Tablet VII:** no fit. No line or gap in the preserved text accommodates *šīmātu* followed by *ina ṣēri aldu*. The superficially similar lines (102–103, 110, 131, 147) fail on spelling, grammar or the surrounding preserved text.
- **Probable attribution:** SB Gilgameš **Tablet I, around ll. 221–223** (Enkidu's boast before going to Uruk).

# K.16980 and Tablet VIII

**Conclusion: the fragment does not plausibly belong to Tablet VIII.** No gap in the Tablet VIII text accommodates its signs, and both of its lines closely parallel two consecutive lines of Tablet I. The scholar's note ("cf. Gilg I 222-223") points the right way.

## 1. What the fragment preserves

- **Line 1:** `[... i?-s]in-nu ši-ma-t[u₂? ...]`
  - The one secure word is *šīmātu*, "destinies".
  - The sign before it is uncertain; *isinnu*, "festival", is only a tentative reading.
- **Line 2:** `[...] x EDIN al-du [...]`
  - This is *ša ina ṣēri aldu*, "(he) who was born in the wild".
  - The note on file rightly takes this as an epithet of Enkidu.

Since the lines are consecutive, any placement must match two adjacent lines.

## 2. Searching Tablet VIII

**Enkidu's origins (VIII 3–6).** This is the one passage about Enkidu's birth among the animals. Its wording is quite different:
- "your mother a gazelle, your father a wild donkey i[bnû]ka"
- "urabbûka", "ušēdûka kal merêti"
- Every line is preserved or securely restored in at least one manuscript.
- There is no room for *aldu*, and *šīmātu* does not occur.

**"Festival" (VIII 48).** *lubār isinnātīya* is fully preserved in NinNA2 ii 6. It is part of a list of Gilgameš's lost possessions. It is not followed by anything like *ina ṣēri aldu*.

**VIII 208.** NinNA2 v 2' has `[...]-du#-tu ša₂ ni-id-[...]`. This ends in *-dutu*, not *aldu*, and the context (a speech about the judge of the Anunnaki) does not fit.

**Lost sections (78–83, 186–198, 220–228, 231–249):**
- 186–198 belongs to the offerings sequence. It is rigidly formulaic ("for DN … he displayed to Šamaš"; "may DN receive this … and walk at his side"). A pair like "…destinies / …born in the wild" does not fit that pattern.
- 78–83 and the tablet's end are too poorly known to exclude the fragment outright. However, there is no positive evidence for it there, and a better placement exists elsewhere.

## 3. The Tablet I parallel

SB I 222–223 comes from Enkidu's boast to Šamhat before going to Uruk. In George's reconstruction it runs roughly:

- I 222: "…[I will go in and] change the destinies (*šīmāti lušanni*)"
- I 223: "[He who] was born in the wild (*ša ina ṣēri aldu*) is [mighty], strength he has!"

The fragment matches this on three points:
- **Consecutive lines:** *šīmātu* in line 1 and *ṣēri aldu* in line 2 fall on adjacent lines, as in I 222–223.
- **Line 2:** EDIN *al-du* matches I 223 exactly.
- **Line 1:** *ši-ma-t[u₂]* corresponds to *šīmāti* in I 222. The sign read "*i?-s]in-nu*" should probably be re-collated. It may belong to a form of *šanû*, "to change", such as `[... -ša]n-nu`, perhaps written in a different order or as a variant, rather than to *isinnu*.

## Verdict

- K.16980 fits no gap in Tablet VIII.
- It should be assigned to **Tablet I, lines 222–223** (Enkidu's boast), as a further Kuyunjik manuscript of that passage, or else to a text quoting it.
- Line 1's first sign needs collation to confirm the reading against I 222.
